title: The proportionator: unbiased stereological estimation using biased automatic image analysis and non-uniform probability proportional to size sampling
authors: Gardi JE, Nyengaard JR, Gundersen HJG
one_line_what_it_does: Tiles a tissue section into fields of view, weights each by an automatic image-analysis proxy for the target structure, samples fields with probability proportional to weight (PPS), and gets a design-unbiased whole-section total regardless of how biased the proxy is; reports 2-15x efficiency vs systematic uniform random sampling.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Core of the claim (cheap image-derived prediction guides random placement of expensive measurement windows; unbiased by known inclusion probabilities; efficiency depends on proxy quality). Differs: counts not expression; tiles from a fixed lattice; weight ∝ proxy size not ∝ residual SD; HT not difference estimator; no PPI.

title: Automatic sampling for unbiased and efficient stereological estimation using the proportionator in biological studies
authors: Gardi JE, Nyengaard JR, Gundersen HJG
one_line_what_it_does: Applied proportionator: region of interest partitioned into fields of view, each weighted by image-analysis feature amount, fields sampled with known probabilities proportional to weight; shown in several tissues.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Same as above; the practical biomedical form (histological sections, tile-based windows).

title: The smooth fractionator
one_line_what_it_does: Fractionator sampling in which each item gets a possibly biased 'guesstimate' correlated with its content; items are ordered by it before systematic sampling to cut variance; unbiased and gives unbiased precision estimates via independent sub-samplings.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Precursor of using a biased auxiliary to improve unbiased window sampling; ordering rather than PPS; independent replicate samplings give variance estimate (relevant to one-window-per-slide variance estimation).

title: Using biased image analysis for improving unbiased stereological number estimation - a pilot simulation study of the smooth fractionator
authors: Gardi JE, Nyengaard JR, Gundersen HJG
one_line_what_it_does: Simulation of smooth-fractionator sampling guided by crude automatic image analysis vs SURS and SRS.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Shows image-prediction-guided unbiased sampling of fields in sections; no inference theory beyond stereology.

title: Improving efficiency in stereology: a study applying the proportionator and the autodisector on virtual slides
one_line_what_it_does: Exhaustive counts on whole virtual slides used to simulate proportionator vs systematic uniform random sampling.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Retrospective re-sampling of a fully measured slide to compare designs: same evaluation logic as re-windowing fully profiled ST sections.

title: Stereology for Statisticians
one_line_what_it_does: Design-based stereology: systematic sampling, Cavalieri estimator, variance of systematic samples, practical sampling designs.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Textbook basis for randomly placed systematic windows and their variance; publisher blurb only was read (book not read).

title: Design-Based Prediction-Powered Inference for Spatial Data (v1; v2 retitled 'Conditional validity of prediction-powered inference for spatially dependent finite populations')
one_line_what_it_does: PPI recast as design-based difference estimation for a census parameter of a fixed spatial population with wall-to-wall predictions; exact design variances under SRS, stratified and spatially balanced (block-stratified) designs; Prop. 3 anticipated-variance-optimal inclusion probabilities pi_i ∝ sqrt(E_xi[residual^2]) (Poisson) and spatial Neyman allocation using a semivariogram; estimated-propensity sandwich inference; map-dependent selection.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Closest PPI paper: has HT/difference estimator, map-guided selection, anticipated-variance-optimal density ∝ predicted residual magnitude, spatial residual correlation. Differs: units are points/pixels labelled individually (one pixel per block), not contiguous windows with window-induced inclusion probabilities; geospatial (LUCAS/WorldCover), not ST; v1 read in full-text extract (abstract, intro claims, Sec 3, Prop 3, discussion); v2 only abstract.

title: Prediction-Powered Inference with Inverse Probability Weighting
authors: Datta J et al. (Datta and Polson per Shirota 2026 citation)
one_line_what_it_does: Design-based reading of PPI rectifier; Horvitz-Thompson and Hajek corrections for informative labelling; estimated propensities.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: HT-PPI with unequal inclusion probabilities (already in project prior-art list); no windows, no placement design.

title: Spatially Robust Inference with Predicted and Missing at Random Labels
authors: Salerno S, Wu Z, McCormick TH
one_line_what_it_does: Doubly robust cross-fit PPI with MAR labelling and spatial dependence; jackknife-HAC variance.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Spatially dependent PPI with covariate-driven labelling; propensity estimated, no design of placement.

title: PPI is the Difference Estimator: Recognizing the Survey Sampling Roots of Prediction-Powered Inference
one_line_what_it_does: Shows PPI mean = difference estimator, PPI++ = GREG.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Places the estimator part of the claim firmly in survey sampling (Cassel-Sarndal-Wretman 1976).

title: Active Statistical Inference
one_line_what_it_does: Label each unit with probability pi(X) derived from model uncertainty; AIPW estimator with optimal pi ∝ sqrt(E[(Y-f)^2|X]), mixed with uniform.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Design-of-labels part of claim (density ∝ predicted residual scale, design-unbiased); already in project prior-art list; unit-level, i.i.d., no windows.

title: Survey Design Under the Regression Superpopulation Model
one_line_what_it_does: Anticipated variance as design criterion; optimal inclusion probabilities proportional to the model residual standard deviation (Godambe-Joshi bound).
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: The 'choose placement density to minimise design variance' principle for unit-level designs; read via secondary descriptions (abstract on ResearchGate; Tille 2017 Stat Sci and Shirota restate the result).

title: Probability Sampling Designs: Principles for Choice of Design and Balancing
authors: (authors not captured; Tillé is first author per my recollection, unverified in session)
one_line_what_it_does: Reviews model-assisted choice of design: minimise anticipated variance by pi ∝ sigma_eps and balanced sampling on auxiliaries.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: States the general optimal-design recipe (inclusion probs ∝ residual SD + balancing) the claim instantiates.

title: Forest inventory with optimal two-phase two-stage sampling schemes based on the anticipated variance
one_line_what_it_does: Optimal spatial sampling schemes for forest inventory minimising anticipated variance under a local Poisson model; optimal inclusion rules are PPS in one-stage and a combination of 'probability proportional to prediction' and 'proportional to error' in two-stage designs; boundary effects handled in estimation.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Spatial plots (extended supports) with cheap auxiliary prediction and anticipated-variance-optimal inclusion rules: methodological precedent for the 'optimise placement density by anticipated variance' step outside ST. Full text not read (abstract and secondary description only).

title: An extension of the Horvitz-Thompson theorem to point sampling from a continuous universe
one_line_what_it_does: HT-type theory for sampling points/supports from a continuous universe with a sampling density.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Theory for window/plot-induced inclusion densities in continuous domains (placement density -> unit inclusion).

title: Response designs and support regions in sampling continuous domains
one_line_what_it_does: Fixed-shape support region with uniform weights gives an unbiased estimator of the total; near boundaries use differential weights or altered support shape.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Exactly the edge/boundary handling needed when a fixed-size capture window is placed on an irregular tissue outline.

title: Spatially Balanced Sampling of Continuous Populations
one_line_what_it_does: Local pivotal method for well-spread samples in continuous populations to reduce HT variance.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Spatially balanced random placement for the multi-window case (several windows per slide).

title: The continuous population approach to forest inventories and use of information in the design
one_line_what_it_does: Sample points with any prescribed intensity over a continuous population, using remote-sensing auxiliaries via balanced or spatially balanced selection.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Intensity function over a continuous domain guided by full-cover auxiliary information: the 'placement density' object.

title: Efficient sampling strategies for forest inventories by spreading the sample in auxiliary space
authors: Grafstrom A, Saarela S, Ene LT
one_line_what_it_does: With full-cover auxiliary data available at planning, spread the sample in auxiliary space (LPM) to improve design-based and kNN estimation.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Auxiliary-guided probability designs with wall-to-wall predictors (remote sensing) as in histology-guided windows.

title: Circular or square plots in ALS-based forest inventories - does it matter?
one_line_what_it_does: Sampling design built so every location has equal probability of inclusion in a randomly centred circular or square plot, compared in ALS-assisted inventory.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Worked example of window-shape-induced inclusion probabilities under random centre placement.

title: A Tutorial on Model-Assisted Estimation with Application to Forest Inventory
authors: McConville KS, Moisen GG, Frescino TS
one_line_what_it_does: GREG / model-assisted estimation with auxiliary maps for plot data.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Estimator part of claim is standard in forest inventory.

title: Smart spatial omics (S2-omics) optimizes region of interest selection to capture molecular heterogeneity in diverse tissues
venue_or_arxiv: Nat Cell Biol (article s41556-025-01811-w); preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.21.677634
one_line_what_it_does: Uses pathology foundation-model features of an adjacent H&E to cluster the section, then deterministically picks ROIs maximising a representativeness 'ROI score'; supports multi-section selection, positive/negative priors, and an optional whole-slide recovery module; validated on Xenium, Visium HD, CosMx.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Closest ST tool for 'where to place the capture area from H&E'. No randomisation, no inclusion probabilities, no design-unbiased estimator, no variance; selection is purposive, so whole-tissue estimates from the ROI are not design-valid.

title: Benchmarking Active Spot Selection for Cost-Efficient Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: (authors not captured; corresponding author R Deng)
one_line_what_it_does: Retrospective pool-based benchmark of active learning vs uniform random spot selection for ST on HER2+ breast and cSCC; evaluates PCC, cluster agreement, Moran's I.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Retrospective hide-and-reveal evaluation; finds active selection does not consistently beat random at small budgets (bears on expected gain from guided placement); spot-level, predictor-training objective, no inference.

title: SCR2-ST: Combine Single Cell with Spatial Transcriptomics for Efficient Active Sampling via Reinforcement Learning
one_line_what_it_does: Active sampling of ST spots under 10% budgets with RL.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Sampling-design-for-ST for predictor training; no design-based estimation.

title: SpatialFinder: A Human-in-the-Loop Vision-Language Framework for Prioritizing High-Value Regions in Spatial Transcriptomics
one_line_what_it_does: VLM + pathologist feedback to rank informative subregions of histology for targeted ST; evaluates selected subregions against ground-truth spatial omics.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Second ROI-selection tool; purposive, no probabilistic design.

title: Scaling up spatial transcriptomics for large-sized tissues: uncovering cellular-level tissue architecture beyond conventional platforms with iSCALE
one_line_what_it_does: Measures ST only on small 'daughter captures' (e.g. 2x2 mm) of a large 'mother' H&E and predicts expression over the whole section; semi-automatic daughter-capture selection.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Same physical setting (small measured windows, whole-section H&E); prediction-only, no design-unbiased inference.

title: A technical comparison of spatial transcriptomics platforms across six cancer types
one_line_what_it_does: Simulates random sampling of FOV-sized tissue areas from a full Xenium scan and shows composition estimates depend on sampled area, increasing with number of FOVs.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Empirical evidence that window sampling bias/variance for whole-section estimands is a recognised problem; no estimator or design theory.

title: Benchmarking sketching methods on spatial transcriptomics data
one_line_what_it_does: Compares uniform, leverage-score, Geosketch, scSampler subsampling of ST data; expression-guided sampling over-samples high-variability regions.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Shows informative (heterogeneity-guided) subsampling distorts naive summaries - the issue HT weighting removes; not design-based.

title: Sampling design for accuracy assessment of land cover
one_line_what_it_does: Design-based sampling designs (including one-stage cluster sampling of contiguous pixel blocks) for map accuracy and area estimation, with difference/regression estimators.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Map-assisted design-based estimation with contiguous block PSUs and edge effects; precedent for window-as-PSU in map-assisted settings.

title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference
one_line_what_it_does: Cluster-robust PPI++ with fully/partially/un-labelled clusters.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: In project prior-art list; clusters with partially labelled units is the 'window within a slide' case, but placement is not designed.
